title: Serum MPO-DNA Complexes as a Biomarker of Disease Activity in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
off: Serum Myeloperoxidase-DNA Complexes as a Novel Biomarker of Neutrophil Extracellular Trap and Disease Activity in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
summary:
Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by immune system dysregulation and inflammation affecting multiple organs. A key mechanism in its development involves the excessive formation and impaired clearance of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), which release myeloperoxidase-DNA (MPO-DNA) complexes into the circulation. Although standard laboratory markers like complement proteins (C3, C4) and anti-dsDNA antibodies are routinely used, they often show inconsistent sensitivity in monitoring disease activity and flare-ups.

The primary purpose of this observational study is to evaluate serum MPO-DNA complexes as a circulating biomarker of NET formation in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.

The study aims to:

* Measure serum MPO-DNA complex levels in active SLE patients compared to age- and sex-matched inactive SLE controls.
* Assess the correlation between MPO-DNA complex levels and clinical disease activity measured by the SLE Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K) score.
* Evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of MPO-DNA complexes compared to conventional inflammatory and immunological markers (ESR, CRP, C3, C4, and anti-dsDNA).

Participants will undergo routine clinical assessments and standard blood sampling to measure routine laboratory parameters and circulating MPO-DNA complex levels via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) according to the 2019 European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology/American College of Rheumatology (EULAR/ACR) classification criteria.
* Age older than 16 years.
* Provision of written informed consent prior to study enrollment.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Age 16 years or younger.
* Overlapping autoimmune diseases (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, systemic sclerosis, mixed connective tissue disease).
* Concurrent active severe infections.
* Malignancy.
* Pregnancy.

arms.d: Consists of 45 patients clinically diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus according to the 2019 EULAR/ACR classification criteria, presenting with active disease as determined by the Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K). Serum samples are collected to measure circulating myeloperoxidase-DNA (MPO-DNA) complexes via ELISA alongside routine inflammatory and immunological markers.

Consists of 45 age- and sex-matched patients clinically diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus according to the 2019 EULAR/ACR classification criteria, presenting with inactive disease (clinical remission) based on SLEDAI-2K scoring. Serum samples are collected to evaluate baseline circulating MPO-DNA complex levels and routine laboratory parameters for comparative analysis.

x.titre: Complexes MPO-ADN sériques comme marqueur d'activité du lupus systémique
x.question: Les complexes myélopéroxydase-ADN sériques, reflet des NET, sont-ils plus élevés dans le lupus actif et corrélés à son activité ?
x.contexte:
Le suivi de l'activité du lupus repose sur le SLEDAI-2K, le complément (C3, C4) et les anticorps anti-ADN natif, dont la sensibilité pour détecter une poussée est inconstante. Des marqueurs plus proches de la physiopathologie sont donc recherchés.

Un mécanisme clé de la maladie est la formation excessive et l'élimination défaillante des pièges extracellulaires des neutrophiles (NET), qui libèrent dans la circulation des complexes myélopéroxydase-ADN (MPO-ADN). Cette étude observationnelle cas-témoins de l'université d'Assiut (Égypte) compare, chez 90 patients lupiques, 45 patients en maladie active et 45 patients appariés en rémission. Le dosage des complexes MPO-ADN est réalisé par ELISA, en plus des examens de routine. L'étude évalue la corrélation avec le SLEDAI-2K et la précision diagnostique comparée à la VS, la CRP, C3, C4 et les anti-ADN natif.
x.interet: Cette étude pourrait valider un marqueur biologique complémentaire de l'activité du lupus. Un tel marqueur aiderait à détecter les poussées quand les tests habituels sont discordants.
x.profil: Des adultes et adolescents de plus de 16 ans avec un lupus systémique, actif ou en rémission clinique.
exclusion: Autre maladie auto-immune associée (polyarthrite rhumatoïde, sclérodermie, connectivite mixte)

bras.traitement: Prélèvement sanguin : dosage des complexes MPO-ADN et des marqueurs usuels

x.critere: Concentration sérique des complexes MPO-ADN à l'inclusion
